raw_record.question_text: Here is a graph showing the amount of product formed during an enyzyme-mediated reaction. Calculate the mean rate of product formed in the first 90s.

method.method_draft: From the image, first read the product formed at 0 s and at 90 s. The curve starts at 0.00 mg and reaches approximately 0.04 mg at 90 s. Use mean rate = (0.04 - 0.00) mg / (90 - 0) s = 4.4 × 10^-4 mg s^-1, so report 4.4 if the answer field expects the coefficient.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph axes: x-axis is Time (seconds), y-axis is Product formed (mg). From the plotted curve, identify that at t = 0 s the product is about 0.00 mg and at t = 90 s the product is about 0.04 mg.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the requested quantity is the mean rate of product formation during the first 90 s, not the instantaneous rate at 90 s.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the definition of mean rate over an interval: mean rate = change in product formed / change in time. If the expected format is the coefficient, convert 0.04/90 mg s^-1 to 4.4 × 10^-4 mg s^-1, giving 4.4 as the coefficient.

method.method_draft: Use the graph as a slope diagram: draw a chord from the origin of the curve, approximately (0 s, 0.00 mg), to the curve value at 90 s, approximately (90 s, 0.04 mg). Calculate the chord gradient as rise/run = 0.04 mg / 90 s = 4.4 × 10^-4 mg s^-1. If only the leading number is required, give 4.4.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached graph plots Product formed (mg) on the y-axis against Time (seconds) on the x-axis. The curve starts at about (0 s, 0.00 mg). At 90 s, the curve is approximately at 0.04 mg of product formed.
Reasoning: The mean rate over the first 90 s is the chord gradient from the origin to the point at 90 s. Change in product = 0.04 mg − 0.00 mg = 0.04 mg. Change in time = 90 s. Mean rate = 0.04 mg / 90 s = 4.44 × 10^-4 mg s^-1, which gives a leading value of 4.4.

planner_metadata.image_role: On the displayed product-vs-time graph, locate the point on the curve at 90 s, which lies near the 0.04 mg horizontal gridline, and the starting point at the origin. Imagine or draw a straight secant line connecting these two points.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the wording “mean rate ... in the first 90s” to select the secant from 0 to 90 seconds rather than a tangent to the curve.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a product-time graph, the average rate over a time interval equals the gradient of the secant line joining the two endpoints: gradient = vertical rise / horizontal run. Convert the gradient to scientific notation if needed.
